children: The Enforcement Directorate (ED), Bengaluru, has conducted searches at three premises linked to cryptocurrency platforms CoinDCX and Delta Exchange over alleged unauthorised cross-border financial transactions involving crypto derivatives and Real World Asset (RWA) tokens.

In a post on X on November 6, the agency said the searches were conducted under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999. The searches took place on November 4 and 5 at premises linked to Neblio Technologies Pvt. Ltd., which operates CoinDCX, and Excelium Technologies Pvt. Ltd., which operates Delta Exchange India.

According to the ED, both platforms offered spot trading in cryptocurrencies, futures and options in crypto tokens, and trading in tokenised stocks of foreign companies. The agency is examining whether these activities involved unauthorised cross-border transactions.
W
hat has the ED alleged?

The ED's preliminary investigation indicated that customer funds deposited in Indian rupees on CoinDCX were converted into USDT, a stablecoin, and transferred to overseas cryptocurrency exchanges, including Binance, KuCoin and Gate.io, to execute trades.

The agency alleged that these transactions were routed through an account held in the name of a Costa Rica-based entity, which it described as a paper entity. It said the transactions were also executed through CoinDCX's application programming interfaces (APIs).
The agency said the volume of cross-border spot trading transactions ran into thousands of crores of rupees.

The ED also alleged that CoinDCX facilitated cryptocurrency futures and options trades by opening corresponding positions on overseas exchanges, including Binance, KuCoin, Bybit and Gate.io. According to the agency, these positions were linked to customer trades on the Indian platform, with settlements taking place on the overseas exchanges.
Delta Exchange transactions under investigation

The ED alleged that a large volume of futures and options trades and tokenised stock transactions offered by Delta Exchange India were routed through CoinDCX, which then executed corresponding transactions on overseas cryptocurrency exchanges.

The agency said these cross-border transactions involved several thousand crores of rupees. It is also investigating alleged transfers of hundreds of crores of rupees by Delta Exchange India to its overseas associate entities.

The ED is examining the regulatory compliance of products offered by both platforms under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, the SEBI Act, 1992, and the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, among other laws.
The agency said further investigation is underway.
What have CoinDCX and Delta Exchange said?

Responding to the ED's statement, Delta Exchange India said it acknowledged the agency's visit to its premises on November 4 and 5 and had cooperated with officials by providing the information sought.
The company said its operations, including trading, deposits and withdrawals, continued without disruption and that user funds remained secure in Indian banks.

Delta Exchange India said Excelium Technologies had been registered with the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) since 2023 as a reporting entity. It added that it complied with applicable laws and KYC, anti-money laundering (AML) and reporting requirements.
The company also said its business did not involve cross-border transfers of virtual digital assets (VDAs) and that it operated an INR-settled exchange for Indian users.

CoinDCX, meanwhile, said ED officials visited its Bengaluru office on November 4 as part of an enquiry. The company said it had cooperated with the authorities and provided the required information and assistance.

CoinDCX said it was registered with FIU-IND and regularly assisted law enforcement agencies with their enquiries. It added that it operated in compliance with applicable Indian laws, including FEMA, 1999, and followed KYC, AML and reporting requirements.
The company said trading, deposits and withdrawals on its platform remained fully operational.

title: ED searches 3 premises linked to CoinDCX, Delta Exchange in FEMA case
